module.name: ACT Core
module.author: UW DIGI
module.description: The ACT registry's server side: scheduled re-evaluation of every enabled, unretired patient flag, mirrored into patient lists, a look-up of the data missing behind a flag, each patient's prophylaxis adherence and next due date, a download of forms' fields, each recorded, the Logs page's activity, reads and downloads, and loading the report descriptors at startup.

globalProperty.description: The program every newly registered patient is enrolled in, at the session location on the day they are registered, and whose enrolments may not overlap one that is open. Merging two patients folds each overlapping pair into its open enrolment (the earlier, if both are open), dated from the earlier of the two, and voids the other. Leave empty to enrol nobody, for example while migrating ACT 2.0 data; that also stops refusing and folding overlaps.
The retired program each new research study copies its workflows from. A study is a program, other than this one, with a workflow on the same concept as one of this one's.

The person attribute type recording registry consent. A patient is enrolled in a study only when it holds actcore.studies.yesConcept. Leave empty to drop the rule, for example while migrating ACT 2.0 data.

The person attribute type recording whether the patient would like to be considered for research. A patient is enrolled in a study only when it holds actcore.studies.yesConcept. Leave empty to drop the rule.
The Yes answer to registry consent and the research opt-in. Leave empty to drop both rules.
The program attribute type holding a participant's Study ID. A new study enrolment without one is refused. Leave empty to drop the rule.

The concept of the study status a patient's open study enrolments move to, on their death date or the enrolment's latest status date if later, when they are saved as dead. Enrolments already completed keep their status. Leave empty to leave enrolments open.

The roles, by uuid and separated by commas, that an administrator limited to their clinics may give a user: one who may add or edit users but does not hold Task: act.allClinics, which in ACT is the site administrator. By default ACT's Community Clinician, Data Clerk and Clinician. Such an administrator also sees and changes only users who share one of the clinics on their account (the actcore.clinics user property). Leave empty to leave roles to OpenMRS's own rule.

Only flags carrying this tag are mirrored into a patient list. Leave empty to give every enabled flag a list. Useful where some flags are a clinical signal on the chart and are not worth a worklist of their own. A list whose flag loses the tag is kept, emptied.

Only flags carrying this tag can be dismissed, by a user with Task: act.dismissFlags. A dismissed flag is left out of the patient's flags and its list until ACT Core finds that the patient no longer matches it; if they match it again later, it shows again. Leave empty to let every flag be dismissed.

Name of the cohort type given to lists this module creates. The module creates the type if no cohort type has this name, and creates no lists while a voided type has it. Lists created before this value changes keep their original type.
When the patient flag refresh last finished, scheduled or on demand, as an ISO-8601 instant, even if some flags failed in it. The refresh writes it; ACT's admin page reads it.

The obs group, and its member holding the regimen, that records a prophylaxis prescription. The adherence refresh takes the groups of the latest consultation that has any, by its date. Next steps reads the groups of every form, for an injection regimen recording anaphylaxis.
The injection regimens, as regimen answer uuid:days between injections, separated by commas. Any other regimen is treated as oral, whose adherence is the latest estimate.

Regimen answers that prescribe no prophylaxis, as concept uuids separated by commas: None by default. A consultation recording one has no course, so the patient has no regimen, as the registry already reads None.
The member of a prescription group holding the date it started. A prescription without one is left out.
The member of a prescription group holding the date it stopped. A stopped prescription is left out, as ACT 2.0 left it out.
The date an injection was given.
The clinician's oral adherence estimate, in percent. It counts from the form's Date of Adherence Estimate (the property below), else from its encounter's date.

The oral adherence form's Date of Adherence Estimate: the day an oral visit counts from, as the injection date is for a BPG form, so a visit entered later from paper keeps its own date. A form without one counts from its encounter's date. Leave empty to count every form from its encounter's date.

Days after an oral regimen starts that its first oral visit is due, while no oral adherence form has been recorded since the start: 0 makes it due on the start date, so the patient is on the due list and flagged overdue until the first supply is recorded. Leave empty to give such a regimen no due date, as ACT 2.0 did. A BPG regimen's first injection is always due one interval after the start.
The duration of an oral prescription, recorded with the estimate; it sets when oral prophylaxis is next due.
The prescription duration answers, as answer uuid:days, separated by commas.

The date of a consultation. ACT 2.0 recomputed adherence when a consultation was saved, and its nightly run held a batch-entered patient from the latest consultation or injection until the batch interval passed.
How a patient's injections are entered, recorded on the consultation. As in ACT 2.0 the latest consultation's answer counts, and a consultation that leaves it blank means continuous entry.

The batch data entry answers, as answer uuid:days between batches, separated by commas. ACT 2.0's nightly run skipped such a patient until that long had passed since the later of their latest consultation and injection. Any other answer, such as continuous entry, is recomputed nightly.

The encounter type of each next step's form, as key:encounter type uuid, separated by commas. A step is done once an encounter of its type dated today is in the patient's active visit, and it is offered only to a user with Add Encounters and the type's edit privilege. A refer entry names the encounter type that records a referral (it has no form): Refer to clinician is done once one is saved after the finding that raised it.

The flags that raise a next step, as rule:flag uuid: notPrescribed gives the consultation, or Refer to clinician for a user who may not record it, followUp the procedures form, inr the INR review. Read only for a user with View Patient Flags.
How many days ahead a dose due shows as a next step, besides one due today or overdue.
How old the latest echocardiogram may be before a new one is a next step. A patient with none recorded gets one too.
The oral adherence estimate, in percent, below which a consultation is a new next step, until a consultation after it.

Whether the BPG dose step waits for a clinical review: while the patient's consultation or Refer to clinician is to do and listed for the signed-in user, a BPG dose not recorded this visit is left out of the next steps. Patient Information never holds the dose back, and an oral supply never waits. A BPG on hold stays, since it offers no dose. Set to false to list the dose anyway.
The date of an echocardiogram, whose latest value before this visit decides whether an echo is due.

The answer that reports anaphylaxis, on any question of a BPG form or of an injection regimen's prescription, such as its Reason Stopped. The latest BPG form reporting it makes a consultation a new next step and puts the next BPG on hold until a consultation after it. Either way, it also keeps the low oral adherence step from suggesting BPG.
The next INR date, whose latest value dates the INR review step.
The RHD Consultation Visit's Next Consultation Time Amount, whose latest value after its encounter's date, in the period below, dates the next cardiology visit on the patient banner.
The Time Period of the next consultation, answered days, weeks, months or years on the same encounter as its amount.

The patient identifier types, by uuid and comma-separated, that a download leaves out for a user without Task: act.downloadIdentifiers, and gives as columns to one with it. The default is the National ID, External Patient ID and Alternate ID. The ACT ID column is the patient's preferred identifier of any other type.

The person attribute types, by uuid and comma-separated, that a download gives as columns only to a user with Task: act.downloadIdentifiers, besides the names and birth date. The default is the primary and secondary phones, their owners and the consent person.

The questions' concepts, by uuid and comma-separated, whose answers identify the patient: a download leaves them out, and names them in withheld, unless the user has Task: act.downloadIdentifiers and it is not a research download. The default is the RHD Patient Information form's Home Address, Village/Area of Residence, School Name, Additional information to help locate patient and Relocation Area.

The person attribute types holding a patient's clinics, by uuid and comma-separated: the primary care clinic first, then the cardiac clinic. The Logs page names them with a registration and compares them with the clinics on the reader's account (the actcore.clinics user property) to say when a patient opened is at another clinic. The default is Primary Care Clinic and Assigned Cardiac Clinic.
The forms, by uuid and comma-separated, that the patient chart's forms list offers only for a patient whose gender is F, through GET /form?patient=. The default is RHD Pregnancy.
